hook.text: Generic drugs are identical copies — biosimilars are highly similar but never exactly the same. Biology is messy.

buildup.text: Biologics are too complex to copy perfectly — different cell lines produce slightly different glycosylation patterns.

discovery.text: Biosimilar approval requires analytical, functional, and clinical comparisons — proving equivalence is expensive.

twist.text: Biosimilars are 15 to 40% cheaper than originals — not the 90% discount of generic small molecules.

climax.text: Humira biosimilars finally launched in 2023 — breaking the best-selling drug's $20 billion annual monopoly.

punchline.text: Similar but not identical — biosimilars bring biologic prices down, not to the floor.

quiz.question: Why can't biosimilars be exact copies of the original biologic?
options: Patent law prevents exact replication of biologic drugs
Different cell lines and processes produce proteins with slight structural differences
Biosimilar manufacturers deliberately alter the protein to avoid lawsuits
